species.name: Wildebeest
species.region: Southern Kenya: Mara, Athi-Kaputiei and Amboseli
species.blurb: White-bearded wildebeest from three Kenyan populations fitted with GPS collars to compare how far and how directly each one moves across grasslands crossed by roads, fences and towns.

species.region: Northern Botswana: Okavango Delta to Makgadikgadi
species.blurb: Burchell's zebra crossing between the Okavango Delta and the Makgadikgadi grasslands as the rains arrive.

species.name: Mule Deer
species.blurb: GPS-collared mule deer from the Sublette herd, moving each spring and autumn between low sagebrush winter range and mountain summer range.

source.title: Data from: Study "Wyoming Sublette Mule Deer (2018-2020)"
source.dataCitation: Wilde, Luke; Monteith, Kevin L.; Kauffman, Matthew J. (2026) Data from: Study "Wyoming Sublette Mule Deer (2018-2020)". Movebank Data Repository.

species.name: Pronghorn
species.blurb: GPS-collared female pronghorn in the Adobe Town area of southern Wyoming and northern Colorado, a cold, dry sagebrush steppe they share with feral horses and greater sage-grouse.

source.title: Data from: Study "Pronghorn (Antilocapra americana), Wyoming/Colorado, USA"
source.paperCitation: Hennig JD, Scasta JD, Pratt AC, Wanner CP, Beck JL. 2022. Habitat selection and space use overlap between feral horses, pronghorn, and greater sage-grouse in cold arid steppe. J Wildlife Manage. e22329. doi:10.1002/jwmg.22329
source.dataCitation: Beck, Jeffrey L.; Hennig, Jacob D.; Scasta, John D. (2022) Data from: Study "Pronghorn (Antilocapra americana), Wyoming/Colorado, USA". Movebank Data Repository.

species.name: Elk
species.region: Ya Ha Tinda and Banff National Park, Canada
species.blurb: Female elk from the partially migratory Ya Ha Tinda herd beside Banff National Park. Some migrate each year and others stay put, and the same elk can switch strategy from one year to the next.

source.title: Data from: Study "Ya Ha Tinda elk project, Banff National Park, 2001-2020 (females)"
source.paperCitation: Eggeman S, Hebblewhite M, Bohm H, Whittington J, Merril E (2016) Behavioral flexibility in migratory behavior in a long-lived large herbivore. Journal of Animal Ecology 85(3): 785-797. doi:10.1111/1365-2656.12495
source.dataCitation: Hebblewhite, Mark; Merrill, Evelyn; Martin, Hans; Berg, Jodi E.; Bohm, Holger; Eggeman, Scott L. (2020) Data from: Study "Ya Ha Tinda elk project, Banff National Park, 2001-2020 (females)". Movebank Data Repository.

species.region: Eastern North Pacific: California to the Costa Rica Dome
species.blurb: Argos-tagged blue whales off California heading south in winter to Baja California and the Costa Rica Dome, then north again to feed.

species.name: White Stork
species.region: Europe and the Middle East to Africa
species.blurb: Satellite-tracked white storks from nine countries, some followed for a decade, flying to Africa by the western route over Gibraltar or the eastern route over the Bosphorus and Israel.

source.paperCitation: Berthold P, Bossche Wvd, Jakubiec Z, Kaatz C, Kaatz M, Querner U. 2002. Long-term satellite tracking sheds light upon variable migration strategies of White Storks (Ciconia ciconia). J Ornithol. 143. doi:10.1007/BF02465604

species.name: White-fronted Goose
species.blurb: Greater white-fronted geese followed by GPS and satellite tags from their wintering grounds in the Netherlands to breeding grounds in the Russian Arctic, and back.

source.paperCitation: Kölzsch A, Kleyheeg E, Kruckenberg H, Kaatz M, Blasius B (2018) A periodic Markov model to formalise animal migration on a network. Royal Society Open Science 5: 180438. doi:10.1098/rsos.180438

species.blurb: Ospreys from Oregon–Washington, Minnesota, New York and New Jersey tracked by satellite to wintering grounds from Mexico to Brazil.

source.paperCitation: Martell MS, Henny CJ, Nye PE, Solensky MJ (2001) Fall migration routes, timing, and wintering sites of North American ospreys as determined by satellite telemetry. The Condor 103(4): 715–724. doi:10.1650/0010-5422(2001)103[0715:FMRTAW]2.0.CO;2

species.name: Bar-tailed Godwit
species.region: New Zealand, the Yellow Sea and Alaska
species.blurb: Light-level geolocator tracks of godwits from New Zealand: north via the Yellow Sea to Alaska, then a non-stop flight across the Pacific home. Only stopover sites are known, so flights are drawn as straight lines.

source.title: Data from: Study "Bar-tailed Godwit geolocator tracking New Zealand 2013-2014"
source.paperCitation: Lisovski S, Hoye BJ, Conklin JR, Battley PF, Fuller RA, Gosbell KB, Klaassen M, Lee CB, Murray NJ, Bauer S. 2024. Predicting resilience of migratory birds to environmental change. Proc Natl Acad Sci USA. 121(19):e2311146121. https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.2311146121
source.dataCitation: Battley, Phil F.; Lisovski, Simeon; Conklin, Jesse R. (2024) Data from: Study "Bar-tailed Godwit geolocator tracking New Zealand 2013-2014". Movebank Data Repository.

species.region: Chiloé, Chile to the Gulf of Mexico
species.blurb: Hudsonian godwits from Chiloé Island, Chile, satellite-tracked on their northward migration: a days-long flight across more than 7,000 km, mostly over open ocean, to the Gulf of Mexico.
